land.text: the Kingdom of Di (Zhai): 'northern Shaanxi' (Eighteen Kingdoms table)

predecessors.note: Northern Shaanxi was Qin land; Xiang Yu made the Qin general Dong Yi its king in the 206 division. One of the Three Qins with yong and sai.

land.text: the Kingdom of Di (Zhai): 'northern Shaanxi' (Eighteen Kingdoms table)

successors.note: 'Defeated by Liu Bang' (Eighteen Kingdoms table). Dong Yi later defected to Xiang Yu and died in 204; the land stayed Han's.

capitals.name: Gaonu (near Yan'an)
capitals.note: Not on any page opened: neither the Dong Yi nor the Eighteen Kingdoms page names a capital or a territory beyond 'northern Shaanxi'. Gaonu is the traditional seat of the Di king; unverified. The coordinates are modern Yan'an.

rulers.name: Dong Yi
rulers.title: King of Di (Zhai)
rulers.note: 'Dong Yi as the King of Di', a Qin general; he surrendered to Liu Bang, defected to Xiang Yu after Pengcheng and died by suicide at the Si River in 204.

correction.text: belongs to the Qin dynasty, 208-207 (qin-dynasty_-208), not to the Kingdom of Zhai

keyframe_review.note: Not this state's shape: it is the Qin remnant of 208-207 (1,628,171 km2; 7,395 grid cells including all of Zhejiang, Hubei, most of Henan, Anhui and Hunan), which the Qin page's own rulers cover (Qin Er Shi 210-207, Ziying 207, 'Surrender to Liu Bang: 207 BC'). The Kingdom of Zhai is 'northern Shaanxi' and began in 206. The qin-dynasty dossier reviews this shape as its new keyframe qin-dynasty_-208. The Qin infobox gives 2,300,000 km2 for 220 BC, so the shape is below the empire's height, as the rebel states had left.

correction.text: the Kingdom of Di (Zhai): 'northern Shaanxi' (Eighteen Kingdoms table)

keyframe_review.note: Shape unchanged (25,977 km2; 127 grid cells, 84 percent of them in Shaanxi and 15 percent in Shanxi) and it agrees with the table's 'northern Shaanxi'. The years change: the kingdom held 206-205 here, not to 204 (Dong Yi died in 204 but had surrendered and defected earlier). No page gives an area.

region.text: the Kingdom of Di (Zhai): 'northern Shaanxi' (Eighteen Kingdoms table)

ledger.note: 206: Xiang Yu makes Dong Yi King of Di. The Eighteen Kingdoms were 'created by military leader Xiang Yu in 206 BCE'; table: Zhai (Di), Dong Yi, a Qin general, 'northern Shaanxi'. The Dong Yi page: 'Dong Yi as the King of Di' with Zhang Han (Yong) and Sima Xin (Sai), 'collectively known as the Three Qins'.

region.text: the Kingdom of Di (Zhai): 'northern Shaanxi' (Eighteen Kingdoms table)

ledger.note: 205: Liu Bang conquers the Three Qins. Chu-Han Contention page, 205: 'after conquering the Three Qins in the Guanzhong region, Liu Bang advanced to the east' and Sima Xin and Dong Yi surrendered in that section; the Timeline page and the Dong Yi page put the surrender in 206 ('Dong Yi, the King of Di, and Sima Xin, the King of Sai, surrender to Liu Bang'). The kingdom-of-han dossier (ea-01) has the gain in 205. The year is disputed between pages; the land is the table's 'northern Shaanxi'.

region.text: the Kingdom of Di (Zhai): 'northern Shaanxi' (Eighteen Kingdoms table)

ledger.note: 205: the Kingdom of Di ends. 'Defeated by Liu Bang' (Eighteen Kingdoms table). Dong Yi 'defected to Xiang Yu's side' after the Battle of Pengcheng and died in 204 at the Si River, but no page gives him land again.

wars.name: Liu Bang's conquest of the Three Qins

zones.text: the Kingdom of Di (Zhai): 'northern Shaanxi' (Eighteen Kingdoms table)

wars.outcome: Liu Bang's army defeated Zhang Han; Sima Xin and Dong Yi surrendered; the Guanzhong became Han's base.
wars.note: Timeline, 206 BC: 'Zhang Han, the King of Yong, is defeated by Liu Bang's forces and retreats to Feiqiu'; 'Dong Yi, the King of Di, and Sima Xin, the King of Sai, surrender to Liu Bang'. The Chu-Han Contention page dates the conquest by 205.

certainty.note: 'Northern Shaanxi' is the only description of the kingdom's land on the pages.

notes: ONE STATE OR TWO: Cliopatria's 'Zhai' row (208-204) shares Wikidata Q7183 and the Wikipedia title 'Qin dynasty' with the Qin Dynasty row, but its two shapes are different things: zhai_-208 (208-207) is the Qin remnant, reviewed in qin-dynasty as qin-dynasty_-208 and marked wrong here; zhai_-206 (206-204) is the Kingdom of Zhai (Di) of Dong Yi, a state of the Eighteen Kingdoms, which this dossier covers. wikidata is therefore null (Q7183 is the Qin dynasty's). The state's real life: created 206, ended in 205 when Liu Bang conquered the Three Qins (disputed: 206 on the Timeline and Dong Yi pages, 205 on the Chu-Han Contention page; 205 follows the kingdom-of-han dossier); Cliopatria's end in 204 follows Dong Yi's death at the Si River, which was after his surrender. Dong Yi defected to Xiang Yu after the Battle of Pengcheng (205), and no page says whether he held land again, so no occupation or vassal event is recorded. Not on any page: the capital, the boundary, an area, whether the kingdom became Shang Commandery. Page failed: none for this state. Pages beyond the hubs (Eighteen Kingdoms, Chu-Han Contention, Timeline): Dong Yi (Qin dynasty) and Qin dynasty, 2 against a budget of 1-2. Gazetteer: no new names.
